topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic on the initiation and resolution of inflammation within the Biology of Disease course.

topics.label: Pathogen and Damage Recognition Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects microbes and cellular injury through pattern recognition receptors and downstream signaling cascades.

topics.label: Sentinel Cell Activation and Leukocyte Recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated sentinel cells signal endothelial cells to recruit circulating leukocytes into inflamed tissues.

topics.label: Lymphatic Drainage and Adaptive Immune Priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how sentinel cells migrate via the lymphatic system to lymph nodes to initiate adaptive immune responses.

topics.label: Systemic Inflammation and Septic Shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the severe physiological consequences that occur when inflammatory signaling becomes excessively activated throughout the body.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanisms that shut down inflammation, rebuild damaged tissue, and manage persistent triggers through chronic inflammation and granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and announces the topic of the upcoming session.
